icd.name: FMOFP MIL-STD-1553B Bus ICD
icd.revision: First draft, derived from FMOFP/rtAddressConfig.xml and FMOFP/MIL_STD_1553B/message_schemas.py.
Alee's answers 1-3: display addresses accepted; BIT merged into avionics (RT 1), FM fitness and SW configuration folded in as well; bus controller confirmed as its own process. RT 24-26 freed.

Alee's answers 4-10: UDP transport accepted; legacy WEATHER mode dropped as unnecessary; every TBD value defined from the code that uses it; heading and yaw are true. Command parameters nothing consumed were removed.

First partition (flight control): the plant terminal RT 27 and PLANT_SENSORS, relayed to the FCS as FCS_SENSORS; FCS_GCAS_ALERTS and FCS_PERF_STATUS outputs; the relays section, which also makes the BC deliver the MFD's radar commands. Kevin owns the ICD from this revision.

Navigation and flight management partitions: PLANT_GPS pseudoranges, the nav terminal's NAV_SENSORS/NAV_GPS inputs and NAV_SOLUTION; the FMS's relayed inputs (FMS_ATTITUDE_IN, FMS_SENSORS, FMS_NAV_SOLUTION), FMS_FLIGHT_DATA (replacing the FMS_DATA block), FMS_FLIGHT_MODE_CMD, FMS_CONTROL_CMD/STATUS, FMS_ENERGY; FMS_STATUS, FMS_ATTITUDE_STATUS and FMS_NAV_UPDATE_STATUS grown to report what the Python returned. Double-word (32-bit) fields; a producer may be relayed to several consumers. Enums fms_flight_mode, countermeasures_state, targeting_state, weapons_state.

Weather radar partition: PLANT_WEATHER (the simulated storm cells and stratiform area, moved by the plant) relayed to the radar as RDR_WX_WEATHER; RDR_WX_SCAN; the RDR_WX_PRODUCTS block (VIL and precipitation points, storm cells, precipitation areas, wind shear events, turbulence cells of one scan), replacing the RDR_WX_VIL and RDR_WX_PRECIP streams. Block payload layouts: a header and record sections, generated for both sides. Enums precip_type, shear_severity, turbulence_category.

Terrain-following radar partition: the plant gains the terrain (PLANT_TERRAIN, the elevation profile ahead of the aircraft, a block relayed to the radar as RDR_TFR_TERRAIN - the first block relay and the first receive block); the radar gets the aircraft state as RDR_TFR_SENSORS and publishes RDR_TFR_GUIDANCE and the RDR_TFR_ELEVATION block (the assessed profile and the path commands). The flight control computer takes its terrain clearance from the radar (FCS_TERRAIN) instead of the plant: PLANT_SENSORS loses terrain_clearance. Enums clearance_level, terrain_warning, path_reason.

The first displays on the bus. The radar display (RT 15) receives the weather and terrain-following radars' status, scan summary and guidance by relay and their products as receive blocks (DSP_RDR_WX_PRODUCTS, DSP_RDR_TFR_ELEVATION), and is the radars' control panel: the radar commands move from the MFD (MFD_RDR_*_CMD, never implemented) to DSP_RDR_*_CMD. The PFD (RT 11) receives FMS_FLIGHT_DATA, FMS_STATUS and FMS_ATTITUDE_STATUS by relay (PFD_FLIGHT_DATA, PFD_FMS_STATUS, PFD_ATTITUDE_STATUS). A command whose cmd_seq is 0 is no command: an unloaded command subaddress reads as zeros.

The MFD (RT 13) on the bus. Its radar page mirrors the radar display's pictures: the weather and terrain-following radars' status, scan summary and guidance by relay (MFD_RDR_WX_STATUS, MFD_RDR_WX_SCAN, MFD_RDR_TFR_STATUS, MFD_RDR_TFR_GUIDANCE) and their products as receive blocks (MFD_RDR_WX_PRODUCTS, MFD_RDR_TFR_ELEVATION). Its systems page reads the flight computer's GCAS alerts and envelope exceedances (MFD_GCAS_ALERTS, MFD_PERF_STATUS) and its mission page the FMS flight data (MFD_FLIGHT_DATA). It commands nothing.

Display data by broadcast. The radars' status, scan summary, guidance and product blocks, the flight computer's GCAS alerts and exceedances and the FMS's flight data, status and attitude status are relayed once each to address 31 (BCAST_*), and each display accepts the broadcast subaddresses it draws; a terminal stores a broadcast only on an accepted subaddress. The per-display copies of v1.5 and v1.6 (DSP_RDR_*, PFD_*, MFD_*) are removed. The broadcast map: subaddresses 1-10 the radar and flight-control band, 25-27 the flight-management band.

Engine management partition (RT 3). The plant runs the two engines of engineControlUnit.py and publishes their measurements (PLANT_ENGINE), following the engine computer's thrust command (ENG_THRUST_CMD, relayed to it as PLANT_THRUST_CMD). The engine computer receives the FMS thrust lever (ENG_FMS_CONTROL), the engine measurements (ENG_ENGINE_IN) and the FMS flight data by broadcast, runs thrustManagement.py's per-engine thrust, autothrottle and asymmetry logic and fuelControl.py's tanks, fuel lines, transfer policy and fuel monitor, takes ENG_CMD (thrust per engine, autothrottle, fuel transfer) and publishes ENG_STATUS, ENG_ENGINE_STATUS (broadcast to the MFD and to the flight control computer, whose FCS_PERF_STATUS fuel efficiency now comes from it) and ENG_FUEL_STATUS (broadcast to the MFD). The first subsystems to listen to broadcasts: RT 3 hears 31/25, RT 5 hears 31/18. The broadcast map gains the engine band, subaddresses 18-19. Enums engine_command, engine_select, fuel_tank.

terminal.name: Radar computer - weather, TFR, SAR, targeting, AEWC, track fusion
terminal.note: The five radars stay one terminal; each radar is a subaddress, as before. The weather radar is ported in v1.3 (SA 1, 6-7, 18-19), the terrain-following radar in v1.4 (SA 2, 14-15, 20-23) the targeting radar with the track fusion in v1.10 (SA 4, 8-11, 24-25), the AEWC radar in v1.12 (SA 5, 12-13) and the synthetic aperture radar in v1.13 (SA 3, 16-17, 26-27). terminal.name: Multi-function display

Its radar commands moved to the radar display terminal in v1.5; it commands nothing. From v1.11 its targeting page draws the targeting radar's tracks (31/24, 31/20-21)

terminal.name: Engine indicating and crew alerting display

Its hydraulic, electrical and environmental rows read unknown until those terminals exist

terminal.name: Radar display - the radars' pictures and their control panel

terminal.name: Tactical situation display

terminal.name: Defensive systems - RWR, chaff, flare, ECM
Plant model - the simulated aircraft and world (test equipment, not aircraft software)

From v1.4 it also publishes the terrain: the elevation profile ahead of the aircraft (PLANT_TERRAIN), which is what the terrain-following radar's antenna would measure. From v1.8 it also runs the two engines of engineControlUnit.py (PLANT_ENGINE), at the thrust the engine computer commands (PLANT_THRUST_CMD). From v1.10 it also flies the air traffic the targeting and AEWC radars generated (PLANT_TRAFFIC). From v1.13 it also holds the ground scene the synthetic aperture radar images (PLANT_GROUND): roads, a river, a town with its buildings, forests, a lake, and the vehicles and the ship that move

message.title: Weather radar scan summary
message.doc: What the last completed scan found, for the display's header and for anyone who does not reassemble the RDR_WX_PRODUCTS block. While NORMAL in an operating mode the radar sweeps the full circle over 60 minor frames (1.2 s), six azimuth degrees per frame, rendering the volume from the weather truth it latched when the sweep began; the products of a scan are published as one block when the scan completes, and products_version is the block version carrying them. The counts are what was detected before the block's record limits were applied.

message.title: Terrain-following guidance
message.doc: What the terrain-following radar makes of the terrain ahead, from tfr_processor.py: the clearance assessment of the latest profile against the aircraft's altitude (ClearanceManager.assess_profile: the minimum clearance, the advisory level, which latches at the worst level seen until a profile with no advisory at all), the first altitude command of the path optimiser (PathOptimiser.compute_path, flown at the set clearance), and whether any sample carries a terrain warning (tfr_radar._check_terrain_warnings). Every operating mode produces it, as the Python's radar ran both processors whatever its mode. The flight control computer receives it as FCS_TERRAIN; its minimum clearance is what the ground collision avoidance TERRAIN alert tests. Clearances are negative when the terrain is above the aircraft.

The resolution is the size of a native pixel (sar_radar.resolution, 1.0 m); the picture on the bus is sixteen native pixels to a pixel (RDR_SAR_IMAGE), so a finer resolution is a smaller patch of ground seen more closely. SPOTLIGHT stares at the patch abeam to the right of the aircraft when the mode is commanded (a designated point is backlog, README section 12); the other modes image the strip beside the track as the aircraft moves.

message.title: Ground collision avoidance alerts
message.doc: groundCollisionAvoidanceSys.py, evaluated every frame: PULLUP when vertical speed is at or below -4000 ft/min and altitude is below 2000 ft; otherwise SINK_RATE when vertical speed is at or below -2000 ft/min; TERRAIN when the terrain clearance is below 500 ft; ALT_LOW when altitude is below 200 ft and TERRAIN is not set. PULLUP, SINK_RATE and TERRAIN are severity 1 (WARNING); ALT_LOW is severity 2 (CAUTION). The terrain clearance is the terrain-following radar's minimum clearance over the profile ahead (FCS_TERRAIN, from v1.4); while the radar provides none (not operating, no profile, or the message stale) there is no TERRAIN alert and the clearance SSM is NO_COMPUTED_DATA, as the Python's GCAS treated a missing TFR value. The values that drove the decision ride along so a display can show them without another message.

message.doc: performaneMonitoring.py: an exceedance bit is set while the magnitude of the parameter is above its limit - g 9.0, angle of attack 25 deg, roll 60 deg, pitch 45 deg, vertical speed 6000 ft/min. Fuel efficiency is airspeed / (total fuel flow / 60) in nm per kg (performaneMonitoring._compute_fuel_efficiency, 0 when the flow is 0), from the engine computer's ENG_ENGINE_STATUS heard by broadcast (v1.8), and NO_COMPUTED_DATA while that is absent or stale.

message.title: Engine measurements from the plant
message.doc: What the two turbofans' sensors read, from engineControlUnit.py's engine model run in the plant for each engine: N1 = 0.80 x thrust + 18 %, N2 = 0.75 x thrust + 22 %, EGT = 350 + 4.5 x thrust C, fuel flow = 42 x thrust kg/h, oil pressure 60 + 4 sin(0.1 t) psi, oil temperature 92 + 8 sin(0.05 t + 1) C, vibration 0.2 + 0.15 |sin(0.3 t)|, each with the Python's Gaussian noise, and a compressor efficiency that random-walks between 75 and 98 %; stepped at the ECU's 2 Hz, t being simulated seconds. The thrust is what the engine computer commands (PLANT_THRUST_CMD, applied at the next step); until a valid command exists both engines sit at the ECU's starting 70 %. The Python's thrust random-walked because nothing commanded it. Spool-up is not modelled: the thrust is the command (README section 12).

block.title: Weather radar products
block.replaces: weather_radarVILResponse DISPLAY_VIL_DATA weather_radarData radarDataRequest radarDataResponse weather_radarPrecipitationResponse
block.doc: Everything one scan produced, published as one block when the scan completes so a consumer always draws a consistent picture (README section 8). Which sections are filled depends on the mode: SURVEILLANCE fills vil, precip and cells; MAPPING and PRECIPITATION fill precip and areas; WINDSHEAR fills windshear; TURBULENCE fills turbulence. Positions are polar from the aircraft: true azimuth and range. The record limits apply after the selection described in the README (the Python's own limits for the VIL and precipitation points; new for the rest); the counts before the limits are in RDR_WX_SCAN. The segment subaddress is polled every frame, so an 18-segment block arrives in 0.36 s, well inside the 1.2 s scan.

field.name: size

field.name: azimuth_rate

field.name: range_rate
field.doc: Centroid motion since the previous scan

field.name: vertical_development

section.title: Precipitation areas
section.doc: precipitation_analysis.PrecipitationAnalyzer: connected regions above 30 dBZ, with the Marshall-Palmer rate of their mean reflectivity and a type from it; the 12 strongest by reflectivity are reported

field.name: type
field.doc: HAIL above 55 dBZ, HEAVY_RAIN above 45, else RAIN

section.title: Wind shear events
section.doc: weather_processor.WindShearProcessor on the lowest elevation: shear proxy = 0.8 x |azimuthal reflectivity gradient| in kt/nm, an event where that is 15 or more and reflectivity 20 dBZ or more, one per 5x5-bin cluster, in order of severity; the first 20 are reported

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Beam height at the bin: range x tan(lowest elevation)

section.title: Turbulence cells
section.doc: weather_processor.TurbulenceProcessor on the lowest elevation: spectrum width proxy = local 3x3 standard deviation of reflectivity, EDR proxy = 0.3 x width^(2/3) / range_m^(1/3), a cell where EDR is 0.1 or more, reflectivity 15 dBZ or more and width at least 1, one per 4x4-bin cluster, strongest first; the first 20 are reported

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Beam height at the bin: range x tan(lowest elevation)

block.title: Targeting radar tracks
block.doc: targeting_radar._handle_track_request's track data and lock data in one block (v1.10): every track the radar holds that the track filter admits, with the signature analyser's classification and the stealth detector's assessment (target_processor.py), and the lock. Positions are Cartesian metres east, north and up of the aircraft, as the Python's were, velocities relative to the aircraft. The radar associates each detection of RDR_TRAFFIC with the track whose predicted position is nearest within 1 km and starts a new track otherwise; the signal-to-noise ratio is the Python's 30 - 20 log10(range / 1000) dB and a track's confidence snr / 30 limited to 0..1. Republished no more often than every fifteen frames; the five segments take five frames at 25 Hz.

field.name: update_seq
field.doc: Increments (mod 256) with every track update the block reflects

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the tracks were made in; NONE with no tracks when the radar is not operating

field.name: jamming
field.doc: 1 = jamming detected on the locked track

field.name: lock_quality
field.doc: min(1, snr / 30) of the locked track, 0 when negative

field.name: track_id
field.doc: The radar's track number, from 1, kept while the track is held

field.name: classification
field.doc: SignatureAnalyzer's class after its speed and altitude overrides

field.name: threat
field.doc: radar_data_fusion._assess_threat's rule on this track alone; the track filter selects by it

field.name: stealth
field.doc: StealthDetector: P(stealth) above 0.6 and the corrected RCS below 0.1 m2

block.title: Fused air tracks
block.doc: radar_data_fusion.RadarDataFusion's fused track table (v1.10): the targeting radar's tracks (and the AEWC radar's, when it is ported) correlated within 500 m by nearest centroid, heaviest sensor first; merged by sensor weight (targeting 0.8, AEWC 0.7) with a confidence that is the probability union of the sensors, the classification and identity of the heaviest sensor, and the threat of the rule set; track ids carried over from the previous epoch by nearest neighbour within 500 m. An epoch every 25 frames (the Python's 2 Hz). The table is rebuilt from the sensors' current tracks each epoch, so a track a sensor dropped is gone at once; the Python's 30 s ageing never had anything left to age. The five segments take five frames at 25 Hz.

field.name: targeting_present
field.doc: 1 = the targeting radar was operating this epoch

field.name: aewc_present
field.doc: 1 = the AEWC radar was operating this epoch

field.name: track_id
field.doc: The fused track number, kept while a track within 500 m continues it

field.name: confidence
field.doc: 1 - product of (1 - weight) over the contributing sensors

block.title: AEWC tracks and sector scan
block.doc: aewc_radar._handle_track_request's track data and _handle_sector_scan_request's sector data in one block (v1.12): every track the radar holds, classified by its own rule (a cross-section under 0.1 m2 STEALTH, else a speed over 400 m/s FIGHTER, else more than 30 km above or below the aircraft HIGH_ALT, else UNKNOWN), with the signal-to-noise ratio of its radar equation and the confidence snr / 30; and the six 60-degree sectors (azimuth counter-clockwise from east, as the Python measured it) with their scan progress, the tracks detected in each, the priority manager's score and dwell share and the electronic protection's assessment. Positions are Cartesian metres east, north and up of the aircraft. Republished no more often than every 35 frames: its six segments take 30 frames at 10 Hz.

field.name: update_seq
field.doc: Increments (mod 256) with every track update the block reflects

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the tracks were made in; NONE with no tracks when the radar is not operating

field.name: scan_azimuth_start
field.doc: The commanded sector's start (RDR_AEWC_MODE_CMD), relative to the nose

field.name: track_id
field.doc: The radar's track number, from 1, kept while the track is held

field.name: classification
field.doc: The AEWC's own rule: STEALTH, FIGHTER, HIGH_ALT or UNKNOWN

field.name: threat
field.doc: radar_data_fusion._assess_threat's rule on this track alone

field.name: stealth
field.doc: 1 = a cross-section under 0.1 m2, the generator's stealth band

field.name: detected
field.doc: 1 = the last detection succeeded; a stealth track is detected with probability 0.2 x snr / 30, and a missed one keeps its track but leaves the sector counts

field.name: sector
field.doc: The sector of a detected track, 1-6; 0 when not detected or outside the elevation coverage

section.title: Sectors
section.doc: SECTOR_1 to SECTOR_6: 0-60, 60-120, ... degrees counter-clockwise from east, -15 to 45 degrees of elevation

field.name: azimuth_start
field.doc: The sector's first azimuth; it spans 60 degrees

field.name: active_tracks
field.doc: Tracks detected in the sector at the last update

field.name: jammed
field.doc: 1 = the electronic protection flags the sector as jammed

field.name: scan_progress
field.doc: Advances a tenth every second, round and round

field.name: dwell_fraction
field.doc: SectorPriorityManager's share of the radar's time, at least 0.05

field.name: priority_score
field.doc: tracks + 3 x hostile + 0.5 x seconds since the sector was last scanned (never, as in the Python) + 2 when jammed

block.title: TFR elevation profile
block.doc: The terrain profile the radar assessed, sample by sample with its clearance level and terrain warning, and the path optimiser's altitude commands, as tfr_radar.py's elevation profile and terrain warning messages carried them to the display. Sample i is at ground distance i x range_m / (samples - 1) ahead along the heading; the samples are the profile section's records. The block is republished when a new profile has been assessed and at least 15 frames (0.3 s) have passed since the last one, so a 10-segment block always arrives whole; the guidance message carries the latest assessment every frame. An empty profile with mode NONE is published when the radar stops operating.

field.name: profile_seq
field.doc: terrain_seq of the PLANT_TERRAIN profile assessed

field.name: mode
field.doc: Mode the radar was in; NONE with every section empty when not operating

field.name: range_m
field.doc: Ground distance of the last sample

field.name: commands_truncated
field.doc: 1 = the path optimiser produced more commands than the section holds; the nearest are kept

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Aircraft altitude the profile was assessed against

field.name: set_clearance
field.doc: Set clearance the path was computed for

field.name: min_clearance
field.doc: The smallest clearance over the profile

section.title: Assessed terrain profile
section.doc: One record per terrain sample, nearest first: the elevation, the clearance level of that sample against the aircraft's altitude (ClearanceManager), and the terrain warning of that sample (HIGH_TERRAIN above 1500 m, else STEEP_TERRAIN when more than 300 m from 1000 m)

field.name: elevation
field.doc: Terrain height above mean sea level

section.title: Path altitude commands
section.doc: PathOptimiser.compute_path over the samples within the 9260 m look-ahead window: the required altitude is the highest terrain in a sliding window of max(5, n / 10) samples plus the set clearance, rate-limited to 25 m/s of altitude change at the aircraft's speed, a command emitted when it moves by more than 20 m from the last one, and a final CLEARANCE command at the window's end when the last command is below the window's highest terrain plus the set clearance. Nearest first

field.name: altitude
field.doc: Commanded altitude above mean sea level

block.title: SAR image
block.doc: sar_radar._generate_imagery_data's product, made of the plant's ground scene instead of the Python's random bars (v1.13): a 64 x 64 picture of the ground, two pixels per word. The Python formed a 1024 x 1024 image at `resolution` metres per pixel; the bus carries it reduced sixteen-fold on each side (sixty-four-fold in SCANSAR, which trades resolution for swath), so a picture pixel is pixel_size metres of ground and a building shows as the fraction of its pixel it covers. The picture's top edge is farthest along the heading and its columns run to the right of the track. STRIPMAP and SCANSAR picture the strip whose near edge is 2 km to the right of the aircraft, SPOTLIGHT the same patch frozen where the aircraft was when the mode was commanded; INTERFEROMETRIC and DOPPLER_BEAM, which the Python drew as noise, picture the strip. Open ground is 60, speckled (four looks); a lake 6, a road 20, a forest 110, a town 150, a building 220-240, before speckle. An image every 150 frames while the radar operates with a scene and a fix; its sixty-seven segments take 134 frames at 25 Hz. The change regions are sar_processor.ChangeDetector's events against the previous image of the same mode (the log-ratio image, a CFAR threshold of the local mean plus three local standard deviations over an 11 x 11 window, opened and closed, 4-connected regions of at least 10 pixels), the first five of its up to 32; the detector's reference is dropped on a mode change, as its docstring asked and the Python never did. Empty (mode NONE, no pixels) when the radar is not operating.

field.name: image_seq
field.doc: The image's number, 1-255 round and round; 0 with no pixels when the radar is not operating

field.name: mode
field.doc: The mode the image was made in

field.name: changes
field.doc: Significant change regions against the previous image of the same mode (area over 50 pixels, confidence over 0.6), saturating at 15

field.name: resolution
field.doc: The commanded resolution: a native pixel

field.name: pixel_size
field.doc: Ground per picture pixel: 16 native pixels, 64 in SCANSAR

field.name: heading
field.doc: The picture's up direction: the aircraft's true heading when the image was formed (frozen for a spotlight)

field.name: centre_along
field.doc: Of the picture's centre from the aircraft along the heading, when the image was formed

field.name: centre_cross
field.doc: Of the picture's centre from the aircraft to the right of the heading

section.title: Pixels
section.doc: 64 rows of 64, row 0 at the top (farthest along the heading), two pixels per word, the even-numbered column in the high byte; 0 no return, 255 saturated

section.title: Change regions
section.doc: ChangeDetector.process's events in label order, the first five

field.name: row
field.doc: Centroid row (the integer part of the mean)

field.name: confidence
field.doc: min(0.95, 0.5 + 0.3 x |mean log-ratio| + 0.05 x log10 area)

block.title: Terrain profile ahead, from the plant
block.doc: What the terrain-following radar's antenna would measure: the terrain elevation at evenly spaced ground distances ahead of the aircraft along its heading, from the aircraft (sample 0) to range_m (the last sample), 100 samples over 10 km as tfr_radar.py's profile was. The plant samples its terrain, a fixed function of position (fmofp_plant.terrain), at the aircraft's position and heading every fifth of a second; sample i is at distance i x range_m / (samples - 1), the samples being this block's elevation records. The four segments take eight frames at 25 Hz, so a profile is complete at the radar before the next one is published (until v1.10 the block was polled every frame and the profile published ten times a second; the targeting blocks needed that bus time).

field.name: range_m
field.doc: Ground distance of the last sample

section.title: Terrain elevation samples
section.doc: Nearest first; the record count is the sample count

field.name: elevation
field.doc: Terrain height above mean sea level

block.title: Terrain profile as received by the radar
block.doc: The relayed PLANT_TERRAIN: the bus controller writes the plant's descriptor and segments here in the frames it polls them, and the radar reassembles the profile.

block.title: Air traffic around the aircraft, from the plant
block.doc: What the targeting and AEWC radars' antennas would measure of the other aircraft (v1.10): for each, the slant range, true azimuth and elevation from the aircraft, its velocity relative to the aircraft, and its radar cross-section. The traffic itself (fmofp_plant.traffic) is targeting_radar._generate_target's five aircraft and aewc_radar._generate_target's seven, moved by their own velocities and accelerations as _update_targets did and replaced when they leave their generator's range (100 km, 400 km); the aircraft's own motion is subtracted, which the Python never did because its targets lived in a frame glued to the aircraft. Nothing here says what an aircraft is: no class, no stealth flag, no identity; the radars assess that from what they measure. Published five times a second; the four segments take four frames at 25 Hz.

section.title: Targets
section.doc: One per aircraft in the plant's traffic, in the plant's order

field.name: target_id
field.doc: The plant's number for the aircraft, for the tests; a radar associates by position, as it would in the air

field.name: velocity_east
field.doc: Velocity relative to the aircraft, east

field.name: velocity_north
field.doc: Velocity relative to the aircraft, north

field.name: velocity_up
field.doc: Velocity relative to the aircraft, up

block.doc: The relayed PLANT_TRAFFIC, for the targeting and AEWC radars.

block.title: Ground scene for the synthetic aperture radar, from the plant
block.doc: The ground the synthetic aperture radar images (v1.13): the plant's training range (fmofp_plant.ground), laid out along the northbound track from home, as point scatterers (buildings, the vehicles on the roads and the ship on the lake: a square of `size` on a side at a `brightness`), linear features (roads and a river: lines of a `width`) and areas (a lake, forests, a town: discs). Positions are WGS-84, so the radar places them against the navigation it is given; what a feature is does not reach the picture, only its backscatter. The vehicles and the ship move at the plant's walk rate; published once a second (its four segments take 20 frames at 10 Hz).
